newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE welcomes Berisha's Albania government move.
newsitem.headline: OSCE welcomes Berisha's Albania government move.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Monday welcomed Albanian President Sali Berisha's move to form a broad government incorporating the opposition and to hold early elections.
"The chairman-in-office welcomes the initiative by President Berisha to propose a national coaliton government and the holding of general elections.

"The rapid acceptance of this proposal and the conclusion of a political agreement by the parties is a significant move to meet the demands of the situation," chairman Niels Helveg Petersen said in a statement released at the OSCE's headquarters in Vienna.

The OSCE, Europe's top security body, said Berisha's initiative was a "resolute and positive response" to points raised by former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, who travelled as the OSCE's special envoy to Albania on Saturday.
Vranitzky is to present his report in Copenhagen on Wednesday.
"The early restitution of arms and ammunition is particularly important. The OSCE does not accept the use of violent means and calls for its principles to be respected," the statement said.
Berisha and opposition parties signed an agreement this weekend providing for an all-party government and new elections by June under international observation to end more than a month of unrest.
Rebels in the south of Albania hold five major towns. They are refusing to hand over their weapons, which they seized from army depots, until Berisha resigns.
